00:00:00.000 --> 00:00:11.720: A sustained, resonant bell tone begins, low and clear, with a slow, natural decay. No speech, clicks, or volume jumps are present. The tone fills the audio space without interruption.

00:00:11.720 --> 00:00:13.000: The bell tone ends abruptly. A male voice begins speaking, saying: “What is Nirvana?”

00:00:13.000 --> 00:00:28.000: The same male voice continues: “Nirvana is when everything the mind makes comes to a stop, the letting go of everything carried, the thirst ends, nothing pulls you anymore, stopping, going out, like a flame with no fuel. This is peaceful, this is excellent, namely the stilling of all preparations, the relinquishment of all assets, the destruction of craving, detachment, cessation, extinction.”

00:00:28.000 --> 00:00:29.000: A brief pause. No speech, no sound except ambient silence.

00:00:29.000 --> 00:00:31.000: A different male voice begins: “Why don’t I see Nirvana right now?”

00:00:31.000 --> 00:00:54.000: The second male voice continues: “You do not see Nirvana right now, because you imagine a seer and a world, and neither is there. What is called ‘manana’ is the imagining in egoistic terms, imparting reality to illusory things. Only looking is there, nothing worth looking at. Only a seeing is there, nothing to be seen. The law of dependent arising is already implicated. There is therefore no seer apart from the phenomenon of seeing, according to the Tathagata.”

00:00:54.000 --> 00:00:55.000: A brief pause. No speech, no sound except ambient silence.

00:00:55.000 --> 00:00:57.000: A third male voice begins: “What keeps it going?”

00:00:57.000 --> 00:01:08.000: The third male voice continues: “Thirst keeps it going, impelled by that making it into something, it runs towards the mirage, the gap is ignored. What impels one to ignore that gap is thirst. Perception. What impels one to ignore that gap is craving.”

00:01:08.000 --> 00:01:09.000: A brief pause. No speech, no sound except ambient silence.

00:03.000–00:04.000: A male voice begins speaking, clear, mid-range pitch, natural timbre, no distortion. “Why don’t I see nirvana right now?”

00:04.000–00:05.000: The same male voice continues, no pause, no breath interruption. “You do not see nirvana right now, because you imagine a seer and a world, and neither is there.”

00:05.000–00:06.000: Voice continues, same tone, no volume jump, no background noise. “What is called manana is the imagining in egoistic terms, imparting reality to illusory things.”

00:06.000–00:07.000: Voice continues, no interruption. “Only looking is there, nothing worth looking at. Only seeing is there, nothing to be seen.”

00:07.000–00:08.000: Voice continues, no change in delivery. “The law of dependent arising is already implicated. There is therefore no seer apart from the phenomenon of seeing, according to the Tathagata.”

00:08.000–00:09.000: Voice continues, no pause. “Samsara is a whirlpool as far as the ordinary beings caught up in it are concerned.”

00:09.000–00:10.000: Voice continues, no change in pacing or tone. “Now what about the arhats? How is the idea of this whirlpool presented in the case of the arhats?”

00:10.000–00:11.000: Voice continues, no breath or pause. “It is simply said that for them there is no whirling round, for there to be a designation.”

00:11.000–00:12.000: Voice continues, no change. “Pattantesa nati panna panaya. So in their case, there is no whirling round to justify a designation.”

00:12.000–00:13.000: Voice continues, no interruption. “This then is something deeper than the whirlpool itself.”

00:13.000–00:14.000: Voice continues, no change in delivery. “The whirlpool can be pointed out because of its activity, but not so easily the emancipated ones.”

00:14.000–00:15.000: Voice continues, no pause. “And that is why there is so much controversy.”

00:15.000–00:16.000: The voice ends abruptly. No trailing echo, no fade — total silence.

00:16.000–00:20.000: Silence. No speech, no background noise, no ambient sound. No clicks, thumps, or glitches. No synthetic or robotic voice detected. No volume jumps. No speech resumes.

s4.text:
00:00:00.000 --> 00:00:02.500: A single, sustained, high-pitched electronic tone — pure sine wave — plays. No speech, no other sounds.

00:00:02.500 --> 00:00:03.000: The tone ends abruptly. Silence.

00:00:03.000 --> 00:00:03.500: A male voice begins speaking, clear and steady, with no audible background noise or room echo. He says: “How is the sense of self constructed?”

00:00:03.500 --> 00:00:04.000: The voice continues: “The sense of self is constructed like this: when one looks into a mirror, one suddenly becomes self-conscious...”

00:00:04.000 --> 00:00:04.500: The voice continues: “...even with no such notion, the moment one looks, one is suddenly reminded of it, as if to exclaim, ‘Ah, here I am!’”

00:00:04.500 --> 00:00:05.000: The voice continues: “Even if one already has no such notion, the moment one looks into a mirror, one is suddenly reminded of it, as if to exclaim, ‘Ah, here I am!’”

00:00:05.000 --> 00:00:05.500: The voice continues: “This is the gist of what Ven. Punnanamantani Putta is trying to put across through this discourse.”

00:00:05.500 --> 00:00:06.000: The voice continues: “This shows that the conceit ‘I’ arises due to the five grasping groups.”

00:00:06.000 --> 00:00:06.500: The voice continues: “The gist of this paragraph is that the non-manifestative consciousness, which is infinite and all-lustrous, is free from the qualities associated with any of the concepts in the list...”

00:00:06.500 --> 00:00:07.000: The voice continues: “...such as the earthiness of earth and the wateriness of water.”

00:00:07.000 --> 00:00:07.500: The voice continues: “That is to say, it is not under their influence, it does not partake of them, ‘anubhūtam.’”

00:00:07.500 --> 00:00:08.000: The voice continues: “Whatever nature the word attributes to these concepts, whatever reality they invest it with, that is not registered in this non-manifestative consciousness.”

00:00:08.000 --> 00:00:08.500: The voice continues: “That is why this consciousness is said to be uninfluenced by them.”

00:00:08.500 --> 00:00:09.000: The voice continues: “The secret behind this peculiar presentation will emerge when we bring up the proper similes and parables.”

00:00.000–00:02.500: A single, sustained, high-pitched electronic tone, pure and steady, like a sine wave or test tone, plays without modulation or variation. No speech, no background noise, no artifacts.

00:02.500–00:03.000: The tone ends abruptly. No fade, no residual sound — immediate silence.

00:03.000–00:04.000: Silence — no speech, no ambient sound, no clicks or glitches.

00:04.000–00:05.000: A male voice begins speaking, clear and steady, with no noticeable reverb or room tone. He says: “Nirvana is only attained now, in seeing, just the seeing, with no ‘I’ added.”

00:05.000–00:06.000: The same male voice continues: “Then it will not carry you, nothing to stand on, nowhere to land, neither here, nor there, nor in between.”

00:06.000–00:07.000: Voice continues: “This itself is the end of suffering.”

00:07.000–00:08.000: Voice continues: “And when you’re not by it, there will be the seeing, just the seeing, in the heard, just the heard, in the sense, just the sense, in the cognized, just the cognized.”

00:08.000–00:09.000: Voice continues: “Then, by you are not by it. And when you’re not by it, you’re not in it.”

00:09.000–00:10.000: Voice continues: “And when by you are not in it, then by you are neither here, nor there, nor in between.”

00:10.000–00:11.000: Voice continues: “This itself is the end of suffering.”

00:11.000–00:12.000: A brief pause — no speech, no background sound.

00:13.000–00:14.000: Voice continues: “There’s a certain special way in sharpening a razor.”

00:14.000–00:15.000: Voice continues: “I just wanted to explain to those who might not be familiar with it — this is — the Venerable is speaking about the type of razor used in old times and which is still accustomed to be used in the forest tradition, which is like — like — like a long blade and then a handle, and so one has to sharpen it on a stone in order to be able to shave one’s head, which as monastics we have to do very regularly.”

00:15.000–00:16.000: Voice continues: “End of comment.”

- 00:22.000–00:23.000: [brief pause, no speech]
- 00:23.000–00:28.000: “Paramasana, grasping, grabbing, is something like that. What then is the alternative?”
- 00:28.000–00:30.000: [brief pause, no speech]
- 00:30.000–00:37.000: “A more refined and softer approach is required as meant by the term sammasana.”
- 00:37.000–00:38.000: [brief pause, no speech]
- 00:38.000–00:48.000: “There’s a proper mode of doing it. One has to hold the razor in a relaxed way, as if one is going to throw it away. One holds it lightly, ready to let go of it at any time, but of course with mindfulness.”
- 00:48.000–00:49.000: [brief pause, no speech]
- 00:49.000–00:56.000: “The wrist also is not rigid but relaxed. Hand is supple at the joints and easy to swing.”
- 00:56.000–00:57.000: [brief pause, no speech]
- 00:57.000–01:08.000: “Then with that readiness, one sharpens the razor, sliding it smoothly on the stone, first up, up, up, then down, down, down, and then up, down, up, down, up, down.”
- 01:08.000–01:09.000: [brief pause, no speech]
- 01:09.000–01:18.000: “The third combined movement ensures that those parts of the blade still untouched by the stone will also get duly sharpened.”
- 01:18.000–01:19.000: [brief pause, no speech]
- 01:19.000–01:26.000: “Develop the stainless tool and give up the latency to conceit, was the advice the Buddha gave to Venerable Rahula in the Rahula Sutta of the Sutta Nipata.”

00:04.000–00:05.000: The same male voice continues: “Like a flame with no fuel.”

00:05.000–00:06.000: The voice continues: “I am grown cool, extinguished as I am.”
